Intuitive Surgical stock adds Humana executive to its board
sum: Intuitive Surgical will add Aaron Martin, Humana's President of Insurance, to its board of directors effective January 1, 2027. The company announced the appointment on November 2 in a press release from Intuitive Surgical.

Martin is responsible at Humana for strategy, growth, operations and financial performance across the insurer's portfolio. He also serves on Humana's enterprise leadership team and reports to the chief executive.

Before joining Humana, Martin spent almost four years as Amazon's Vice President of Healthcare. The company said he launched Amazon Clinic, a message- and video-based telehealth platform, and built health programs with digital-health companies. Earlier, he was Executive Vice President and Chief Digital Officer at Providence St. Joseph Health, where he led its consumer-facing digital business and founded Providence Ventures.

Intuitive CEO Dave Rosa said Martin's experience at the intersection of payers, providers and patients would help the company expand access to minimally invasive care. Martin said he looked forward to contributing to that effort. Those statements describe the strategic rationale for the appointment, but do not set out a separate financial target.

With Martin's addition, Intuitive's board will expand from 10 to 11 members. The company described the appointment as effective January 1, 2027 and said it is subject to Martin's continued willingness and ability to serve. The release did not announce a committee assignment.

What Has The Market Missed In Intuitive Surgical Stock’s Drop?
sum: For questions about this article or underlying research, email help@trefis.com.

At Intuitive Surgical (ISRG), customers are trading up to the company’s newest surgical robot, the da Vinci 5, and that may be what buyers of the stock are counting on. You probably think of the company as one that grows only as fast as robotic operations do, but its sales grew faster in the third quarter of 2026. Yet the stock lost 22% over the past twelve months, while the S&P 500 returned 12.8%. That is the contradiction. So how far has da Vinci 5 pushed Intuitive Surgical’s sales?

Customers continue to trade up. Worldwide da Vinci system placements rose 28% in the third quarter of 2026, and the da Vinci 5 and the single-port SP system accounted for 65% of them. In the U.S., the company placed 335 systems, up from 263 a year earlier, as more customers converting to the da Vinci 5 signed deals for several robots at once. With that, revenue from systems grew 30% to $769 million.

The newer robots matter for the rest of the business, too. Management said revenue grew 22% in the quarter while procedures grew 15%, tying the gap to more system placements and a richer product mix as the da Vinci 5, SP and Ion become a larger part of sales.

The upgrade has not lifted the average robot price, though. A purchased da Vinci system sold for about $1.6 million on average, flat on a year earlier, because a higher mix of XiR systems offset a higher mix of da Vinci 5, management said.
Can Intuitive Surgical Outrun Its Own Instrument Price Cuts?

That has not been tested yet, because the price cuts have not taken full effect. Instrument and accessory sales reached $1.8 billion in the third quarter, so what Intuitive Surgical earns on each operation matters more than what it earns on each robot. Instrument and accessory revenue per da Vinci procedure rose to about $1,860 from $1,800 a year earlier, mainly on SP procedures and instruments made for da Vinci 5.

Will Trinity Biotech Stock Gain From Its Latest Patent Process?
sum: Trinity Biotech plc TRIB recently provided an update on its continued development of its glucose biosensor technology. Earlier this year, the company was granted a European patent for a novel method that enhances the performance of its glucose biosensor. Recent testing of this patented process has confirmed its effectiveness in improving the performance of the sensor.
Trinity Biotech intends to use this breakthrough process to stabilize and improve the functionality of its glucose biosensor in its next-generation continuous glucose monitor (CGM) technology.

Shares of TRIB went down marginally by 0.05% in pre-market trading today following the news. However, as the company is gaining a high level of synergies from its continued development within the CGM market, this latest development might prove fruitful in strengthening its foothold in this space. Accordingly, we expect market sentiment to recover shortly.

CGMs are small patch-like wearable medical devices that use biosensor wires under the skin to measure glucose in real time. Generally, these devices experience a “run-in” or “settling” period immediately after their insertion. During the run-in period, glucose readings are unreliable.

Trinity Biotech’s patent describes a unique process within the company’s reusable transmitter unit that “conditions” the CGM biosensor wire. This conditioning process significantly reduces this run-in time, enabling reliable measurements more quickly.

Additionally, the conditioning process has demonstrated notable improvements in the accuracy of the CGM device compared to laboratory reference methods for blood glucose testing. The process also improves the biosensor’s mean absolute relative difference, which is the standard measure of accuracy used to compare CGM devices.

The technology covered by this patent represents a major advancement for the company’s CGM platform. The CGM technology, which Trinity Biotech acquired in January, has a unique self-inserted biosensor wire.It poses strong advantages in terms of affordability and sustainability.

Intuitive Surgical (ISRG) stock would have to rise another 49% from its November 5, 2026 close to reach $700. The maker of da Vinci systems would mainly need continued revenue growth to hit that mark, following a 20.5% increase over the twelve months to September 2026. After a 23.7% gain over the past three months, how much could three more years of owning the shares still make you?

A Trefis scenario built on Intuitive’s own figures values the shares at about $835 three years from now, placing the stock above $700 and 78.2% above the November 5 close. The table below compares the company today against that three-year projection.

Higher revenue accounts for most of that gain, at 83.2%. The instruments and accessories surgeons use in each da Vinci procedure make up the largest part of the business, representing 59.8% of fiscal 2025 revenue.

The scenario also assumes a slightly higher P/E in year three. Because today’s multiple sits well below the stock’s 66.1 average at fiscal quarter-ends over the past three years, the model moves the P/E 40% of the way toward that mark.

Sales outgrew procedures in the third quarter of 2026, when revenue rose 22% and total procedures grew 15%. Management said the shift toward da Vinci 5 and SP is left out of that estimate and will add to revenue per procedure. Intuitive Surgical stock weighs strong growth against legal charge
sum: Intuitive Surgical reported strong operating growth for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026, but a proposed antitrust settlement weighed heavily on reported earnings. The company disclosed the results and legal agreement on October 20 in a SEC filing.

Revenue increased 22 percent to 3.05 billion US dollars from 2.51 billion US dollars a year earlier. The main recurring revenue stream, instruments and accessories, grew 18 percent to 1.80 billion US dollars. Systems revenue rose to 769 million US dollars from 590 million US dollars as placements increased.

Worldwide procedures across the da Vinci and Ion platforms grew approximately 15 percent year over year. Da Vinci procedures increased approximately 14 percent, while Ion procedures advanced approximately 31 percent. Intuitive placed 546 da Vinci systems, compared with 427 in the prior-year quarter, including 315 da Vinci 5 systems against 240 a year earlier.

The installed base also expanded. Da Vinci systems reached 12,094 at September 30, up 12 percent from 10,763 a year earlier. The Ion installed base rose 21 percent to 1,152 systems. Intuitive said customers performed more than 10,000 procedures per day on average during the quarter.

GAAP net income attributable to Intuitive Surgical fell to 523 million US dollars, or 1.49 US dollars per diluted share, from 704 million US dollars, or 1.95 US dollars per share, in the third quarter of 2025. The result included a 450 million US-dollar pre-tax charge tied to a proposed settlement of previously disclosed antitrust class-action litigation.

The agreement covers claims concerning servicing of da Vinci systems and EndoWrist instruments. Intuitive said it made no admission of liability or wrongdoing. The settlement remains subject to preliminary and final court approval, so its final legal and financial status is not yet settled.

On a non-GAAP basis, which excludes the litigation charge and other specified items, net income rose to 1.05 billion US dollars, or 3.00 US dollars per diluted share, from 867 million US dollars, or 2.40 US dollars per share. The contrast highlights the difference between the company's underlying operating momentum and the one-time legal burden.

sum: Shares of Intuitive Surgical (NASDAQ: ISRG) fell after the surgical robotics company reported earnings on Oct. 20. That drop came despite a 22% revenue jump. The real story that investors are missing is that sales of the da Vinci surgical robot aren't the main driver of the company's revenue. Here's what is.

The big concern about surgical robotics right now is that competition is heating up. Medtronic (NYSE: MDT) and Johnson & Johnson (NYSE: JNJ) have each entered the fray. Both are well-respected medical device makers, so they are likely to gain traction with devices that compete against Intuitive Surgical's da Vinci system. Investors appear to view this as a material threat to Intuitive Surgical's growth prospects.

It is, but there's ample room for growth even with new entrants. Notably, Intuitive Surgical sold more da Vinci systems in the third quarter of 2026 than it did in the same quarter of 2025. So, despite new players, growth hasn't stopped. And, notably, the number of procedures using a da Vinci system rose by 15%, while the number of installed systems increased by "only" 12% year over year.

The fact that procedures are increasing faster than robot sales is important to understand, because it highlights the demand for robotic surgery. It also leans into one of Intuitive Surgical's largest strengths. The sale of robots accounts for roughly 25% of revenues, while the sale of instruments, accessories, and services makes up the rest of the top line. So while selling da Vinci systems is important, the real business driver is what amounts to parts and services.

To be fair, Intuitive Surgical's stock price has recovered from the earnings-related drop, and then some. But that drop highlights an ongoing perception issue. While new competition will likely be a business headwind, Intuitive Surgical's already large installed base of over 12,000 systems has created an annuity-like cash flow machine to support the company's business.

David Roman, an analyst at Goldman Sachs (GS), is among them. He recently maintained a “Buy” rating on the stock and set a 12-month target price of $558, which is 47% above Intuitive Surgical’s current share price.

The recent headwinds facing Intuitive Surgical include lower-than-expected profit margins related to the “Da Vinci 5,” the latest version of the da Vinci surgical robot system launched in 2024. The system has seen strong market acceptance, but its profit margins are lower than those of its predecessor. In addition, this medical device specialist is also grappling with rising costs stemming from high tariffs. It remains unclear whether the company can resolve these challenges within the next 6 to 12 months.

Nevertheless, there are solid reasons to be optimistic about Intuitive Surgical’s long-term prospects. Take the Da Vinci 5, for example. This new product offers multiple advantages over its predecessor, among which force feedback technology allows surgeons to perceive tissue pressure and texture through the robotic manipulator, providing better tactile sensation and helping to make delicate surgeries safer, more precise, and easier to perform. With these enhanced features, the Da Vinci 5 is expected to attract surgeons or hospitals that were previously hesitant to use the da Vinci system, thereby helping the company expand its market and potentially gain indications that previous generations could not obtain. This would lead to a larger installed base, as well as stronger and more profitable recurring revenue from instruments and accessories.

Intuitive Surgical still has a substantial addressable market in the robotic-assisted surgery (RAS) industry. Robotic-assisted surgery enables surgeons to perform minimally invasive procedures that offer significant advantages over open surgery, yet market penetration remains insufficient, and with the global population aging, the market is expected to grow further.

sum: Ken Griffin, the billionaire CEO of the investment firm Citadel Advisors, has an impeccable reputation on Wall Street, having delivered superior returns over the long run. It's no wonder, then, that every move he and his team make is carefully scrutinized. And he was a busy man during the first quarter. Citadel Advisors decreased its stake in some popular artificial intelligence (AI) stocks. The firm sold 2.9 million shares of Nvidia (NVDA +2.77%), while offloading six million shares of Amazon (AMZN -0.35%).

Both tech leaders remain among Citadel Advisors' largest holdings, but perhaps the decision to reduce its stake in these companies was to reallocate capital into attractive opportunities. And one notable stock that Citadel Advisors bought during the quarter looks like such an opportunity.

Intuitive Surgical (ISRG -3.35%) has lagged the market recently. The company is dealing with headwinds from multiple sources. Let's consider three of them. First, Intuitive Surgical will face increased competition in the robotic-assisted surgery (RAS) market moving forward. Last year, Medtronic earned approval for a competing system, the Hugo, while Johnson & Johnson is also racing toward clearance of its own device, the Ottava.

Second, several of Intuitive Surgical's products, including its da Vinci 5 -- the newest model of its famous, market-leading da Vinci system -- carry lower margins than the company's average. Selling more of these platforms can drag down margins, at least in the short term. Third, steep tariffs have impacted Intuitive Surgical's financial results. Because of all these factors -- and despite pretty strong financial results -- the stock has dropped by 20% over the past 12 months.

Given all the problems Intuitive Surgical is facing, why did Citadel Advisors take this opportunity to increase its stake in the company by 30.3% during the first quarter? One likely answer is that, despite the medical device specialist's struggles, its long-term prospects remain bright, and it could deliver superior returns, especially at current levels. None of Intuitive Surgical's obstacles is anywhere near insurmountable.

sum: Intuitive Surgical (ISRG +1.57%) has faced significant challenges over the past year, especially related to tariffs. The company's shares have lagged broader equities as a result, and with the trade war still not over, the medical device specialist's near-term prospects look dim. However, Intuitive Surgical does have qualities that could help it overcome its challenges and perform well over the long run. Is the stock worth buying right now? Let's consider both sides of the argument in a little more detail.

Intuitive Surgical's financial results still look pretty good. In the fourth quarter, the company's revenue increased by 19% year over year to $2.87 billion, while its adjusted earnings per share climbed 14.5% to $2.53. All that on the back of a 17% increase in procedures performed with its crown jewel, the da Vinci surgical system, whose installed base during the period also jumped by 12% year over year to 11,106.

Here's the problem. The impact of tariffs on Intuitive Surgical's financial results could get worse over time. Meanwhile, the company is facing increased competition from other medical device makers in the robotic-assisted surgery (RAS) market, as Medtronic recently received clearance for its Hugo system, and Johnson & Johnson could also launch its own system relatively soon.

Amid all that, Intuitive Surgical is still trading at 47.6 times forward earnings, compared to the average forward price-to-earnings of 17.1 for healthcare stocks. Intuitive Surgical arguably deserved a premium so long as it had little competition and tariffs did not significantly impact its results. Now that things have changed, many investors wonder whether the stock is worth it at current levels, or if, given its valuation, Intuitive Surgical's stock could fall even further.

The RAS market should expand over the next decade, as it is currently underpenetrated, even as robot-assisted devices enable minimally invasive surgeries with significant advantages over open surgeries. The former are performed with small instruments that avoid cutting the skin open to have direct access to internal organs. The results are often less bleeding, less scarring, and faster patient recoveries.
